subject.title: Compaction should use auth-profile rotation / failover within the same provider

question: Should compaction inherit same-provider auto auth-profile rotation using an apply-once stable transcript boundary, or should compaction remain single-profile until a broader compaction job model exists?
rationale: The requested behavior matches the existing run-time auth-profile contract, but compaction retries touch session-state correctness and auth-provider routing, so the permanent retry boundary should be maintainer-approved before the linked PR lands.

options.title: Adopt bounded same-provider rotation
options.body: Review the linked PR or an equivalent replacement that rotates only auto-selected profiles and guards against stale or double-applied compaction results.

options.title: Keep compaction single-profile for now
options.body: Leave the issue open as a known limitation and require a broader compaction job design before enabling profile rotation.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics only
options.body: Improve user-visible compaction failure reporting now and defer automatic retry behavior to a later design discussion.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded same-provider rotation
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR or an equivalent replacement that rotates only auto-selected profiles and guards against stale or double-applied compaction results.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction ownership work makes this the best available routing candidate for the session-state boundary decision.
